Diminutivos & aumentativos — cafezinho, carrão

Brazilian Portuguese grammar, chapter 54 of 60 · taught in Lição 34 · level B2. Almost never about size: affection, politeness, sarcasm, intensity.
⌂ Menu Diminutivos & aumentativos — cafezinho, carrão

What this is about

Textbooks say -inho means "small". In Brazil it almost never does. The diminutive is a tone of voice that you glue onto a word: it softens a request, warms a greeting, shrinks bad news, and — the part that surprises everyone — it can also intensify. Cedinho is earlier than cedo. A cafezinho can come in a big mug. Learn the suffix as a social instrument and half of Brazilian warmth becomes available to you.

The form — one question decides it

Does the word end in an unstressed vowel? Drop that vowel, add -inho / -inha. Does it end in a stressed vowel, in -e, or in a consonant? Keep the whole word, add -zinho / -zinha.

casa → casinha · pouco → pouquinho unstressed final vowel → -inho
café → cafézinho · pé → pézinho stressed final vowel → -zinho
mãe → mãezinha · flor → florzinha -e or a consonant → -zinho
amigo → amiguinho · taça → tacinhaspelling shifts so the SOUND never changes
Ear test, two seconds: say the word slowly. If your voice lands on the last syllable — or the word ends in -e or a consonant — glue on -zinho. Otherwise chop the last vowel and add -inho.

The five jobs — none of them "small"

Só um minutinho, amorzinho! affection / politeness
Posso fazer uma perguntinha? softening a request
Relaxa, é só um probleminha.downplaying — damage control
Acordei cedinho e estava quentinho. INTENSITY: cedinho = earlier than cedo
Ah, que gracinha…sarcasm — tone decides
The intensity job: juntinho is closer than junto, agorinha is more urgent than agora, rapidinho is faster than rápido. The suffix that means "little" also means "very". Only context tells you which.

The augmentative — -ão, -zão, -ona, -aço

Que carrão! · Que golaço! size, but mostly admiration
Valeu, amigão! affection between men
Quero um cafezão.-zão when the word needs a buffer
a mulherona · o gordão · o chatão⚠ on people this wounds far more easily than you expect
The safe split: praise a thing with -ão (carrão, festão, golaço); praise a person with -inho. Bodies and the augmentative are a bad combination.

Exceptions & details

1 · Frozen diminutives are separate words. cafezinho is the hospitality ritual, pãozinho is the bread roll, cervejinha is the social beer, festinha is the informal party, jeitinho is a whole cultural concept. Do not translate them as "small X" — learn them whole.
2 · Plurals move the -z-: cafezinhos, florzinhas, but the -ão words behave like their root: pãozinho → pãezinhos.
3 · The diminutive as damage control. When a Brazilian mentions um probleminha, um atrasinho or uma continha, the suffix is being kind, not precise. Ask politely for the number, the date, the detail.
4 · It softens a no. Estou meio ocupadinho agora is a refusal wearing a smile; dou uma passadinha is a modest offer of help.
5 · Never in a formal e-mail. Gostaria de fazer uma pergunta — not uma perguntinha rapidinho. Charm in speech, noise on paper.
